newsitem.title: CROATIA: Tudjman starts campaign for presidential polls.
newsitem.headline: Tudjman starts campaign for presidential polls.

text.p: Croatia's ailing President Franjo Tudjman started his campaign for the June 15 presidential election on Wednesday, saying he would continue the policy that led Croatia to independence from federal Yugoslavia.
Tudjman, 75 and reportedly ill with cancer, is widely expected to defeat his opponents and secure a second term in office in the first round of voting.

The strongman president presented his programme to an elite audience of Croatia's political, economic and cultural leaders in a baroque courtyard in downtown Zagreb, decorated with the slogan 'President for President".
"First and foremost I feel I must secure the continuity of the policy with which we established the independent Croatia and defended its sovereignty," Tudjman said to huge applause.
The only two opposition candidates who managed to secure enough support from voters to qualify for the election, also started their campaigns in Zagreb on Wednesday.

Social Liberal Vlado Gotovac, a poet and former dissident, and Zdravko Tomac of the Social Democrats, said they were fighting against all odds to offer a new vision for the future, including better care for social and economic issues.

None of the three candidates referred to the trouble-ridden issue of the return of minority Serbs displaced by 1991-95 war, on which the West has conditioned Croatia's future access to NATO and the European Union.

"Our daily concern must be the strengthening of Croatia's position abroad and our acceptance accepted into the European Union. But we must keep in mind our national and state interests," Tudjman said.
